wording: Among 105 travellers treated for high-altitude illness at Mustang district hospital (Nepal), 74% had acute mountain sickness (61% mild, 36% moderate, 3% severe); in a Bayesian ordered logistic model of severity (None, Mild, Moderate or Severe), faster ascent rate (km/day) was associated with greater severity (coefficient 1.14, odds ratio 3.13) and smoking with less (odds ratio 0.16). P88's counterfactual says a 1-day Pokhara-Muktinath trip (2978 m gain) doubles the risk of moderate or severe AMS compared with 3 days.
locator: P88 Abstract to Conclusion, Table 2, Fig. 2, peer-review history (read in full; supplementary tables not read)
confidence: Low-moderate (105 hospital patients, cross-sectional, no comparison group without symptoms reaching hospital)
counterevidence_limits: Hospital register sample (P88 notes selection by Thorong La and airlift of severe cases); one site; credible intervals reported as 99% for headline effects. P88 calls the 2.069 counterfactual 'odds' in Fig. 2 and 'risk' in the abstract; see AS0-APP-02.
operationalization: APP Ascendence = ascent to altitude and ascent rate
verification_phrases: P88|None, Mild, and Moderate or Severe || P88|ascent rate (odds ratio 3.13) || P88|is twice that of making the ascent in three days

wording: P88's odds ratios, counts and test statistics reproduce (exp(1.14) = 3.127, exp(-1.82) = 0.162; 78 = 48 + 28 + 2; chi-square p 0.038, 0.0155, 8e-5; SpO2 t p 0.2245). Model-4 point estimates with natural logs give P(moderate or severe) 0.873 for one day and 0.417 for three days, a risk ratio of 2.095 against the printed 2.069 (log10 gives 1.78), so 2.069 is a risk (probability) ratio; the corresponding odds ratio is 9.6, so the Fig. 2 wording 'odds ... increase twofold (2.069)' is not supported.
counterevidence_limits: Point estimates rather than P88's posterior; the natural-log reading of '(Log)' is the agent's assumption.
operationalization: APP Ascendence = auditing an ascent-rate study
